hold_ttl_min.source: spec §8 Bookings: a hold lasts 60 real minutes, never demo time (FLOW-05)
hold_ttl_min.note: env HOLD_TTL_MIN overrides it at deploy

timeout_s.source: 04-CONTEXT Claude's Discretion, engine worker hang rule (OPS-06)
timeout_s.note: well above the 3 s case budget, which stays the api.bench gate and is never raised; env ENGINE_TIMEOUT_S overrides it at deploy

queue_wait_s.source: 04-RESEARCH Pitfall 1: a bounded wait for the one engine slot, then 503 engine_busy

signal.note: field reports successfully filed, per workspace (scope run:<run_id>), shared by every account and store in it; moved from caps.session

upload.source: 07-CONTEXT D-20; FLOW-11; spec §4 Caps (reports with a file)
upload.note: a report's first file, per workspace (scope run:<run_id>); a replacement or an answer photo spends only caps.global.upload; moved from caps.session

preview.source: 07-20 review (2026-10-18): a preview runs the engine (up to reports.preview_cases what-ifs, within the 3 s case budget) on the one engine worker every workspace shares
preview.note: impact previews (draft and filed), per workspace (scope run:<run_id>); spent once before the first engine run, never for a preview whose what-ifs are already stored (read back); filing keeps its own allowance

passcode.source: 06-CONTEXT D-24 (replaces 04-REVIEW WR-03's 20 per hour): wrong passcode attempts, counted per address
passcode.note: only a wrong passcode counts; the address is stored as a hash; on Cloud Run it is the rightmost X-Forwarded-For entry (the one Google's front end appends), locally the TCP peer; after 10 wrong guesses within one clock minute a block lasts until that minute ends (at most 60 s) and is never permanent; visitors behind one shared NAT or VPN exit share a counter (accepted, D-24)

ai.note: requests, not dollars (06-CONTEXT D-13): live questions, live briefs and AI signal analysis share it; cached briefs and manual counts do not spend it (04-CONTEXT D-20); resets at midnight Asia/Bangkok; env GLOBAL_AI_CAP overrides it at deploy

preview.source: 07-20 review (2026-10-18): a preview runs the engine (up to reports.preview_cases what-ifs, within the 3 s case budget) on the one engine worker every workspace shares
preview.note: so one workspace's previews never fill the engine for another's decisions: at most 12 previews of at most 3 s each in a minute, across every workspace

time_zone.source: spec §4: daily caps reset at midnight Bangkok time

retired_sandbox_hours.source: 04-REVIEW IN-01 (agy F-T5-03): a sandbox retired longer ago than this is no session's; its rows and keys go

session_key_days.source: 04-REVIEW IN-01: the ss_session cookie lives 30 days (app.COOKIE_MAX_AGE_S), so an older session-scoped key has no session left to retry it

usage_window_days.source: 04-REVIEW IN-01: a cap window (an hour or a day) older than this is never counted again

engine_cache_days.source: 04-REVIEW IN-01: an older cached result is computed again on its next use (results are deterministic)

runs_per_batch.source: 04-REVIEW IN-01: one bounded batch per reset or new session (no background work on Cloud Run), well inside the 2 s reset target

rows_per_batch.source: 04-REVIEW IN-01: the bound on each shared-table delete in one batch

max_body_bytes.source: 04-REVIEW WR-02 (agy F-T5-01): the JSON or form body is read up to this bound, before the passcode check
max_body_bytes.note: the demo path's bodies are a few hundred bytes; a larger one is 400 bad_request

max_bytes.source: spec §4, §7: PNG, JPEG or PDF up to 5 MB; 07-CONTEXT D-14
max_bytes.note: a larger file part is 413 too_large

form_bytes.source: the form fields beside one file (research F-5)
form_bytes.note: an upload route reads a body of up to max_bytes + form_bytes; every other route keeps http.max_body_bytes

max_message_chars.source: Phase 09 dated API contract: bounded evidence wording
max_message_chars.note: initial application text policy, not a retailer value; shared by checked drafts and the later human Send extension

lead_min.note: a count request is due this long before decide_by

max_per_version.source: spec §7; 04-CONTEXT D-20 (count requests share the limit)

response_min.source: 07-CONTEXT D-05: a real deadline 60 minutes after a request is created
response_min.note: replaces the simulated due time for state; lead_min only fills the legacy due_day/due_min

preview_cases.source: spec §7 step 4; 07-CONTEXT D-16: up to 5 cases in the preview
preview_cases.note: the impact preview re-runs at most this many affected live cases as what-ifs (case_id order) and counts the rest; the display's limit only: confirmation acts on every affected case

urgency_bands.unit: days left (expiry day minus today); each edge starts a more urgent band at or below it
urgency_bands.source: 07-CONTEXT D-28 (user, 2026-10-17, refined): urgency bands are provisional and configurable; a band crossing reopens a closed lot only when it changes the available action
urgency_bands.note: edges: within 3 days, tomorrow, today; provisional defaults, pending retailer; recorded and logged, never a reopen reason on their own; distinct whole numbers of 0 or more, in descending order

clearance_pct.source: 07-CONTEXT D-28 (user, 2026-10-17, refined): crossing a configured clearance or final-action threshold reopens a closed lot on the synthetic Next day
clearance_pct.note: pending retailer: the seeded markdown schedules mark no clearance step and no policy holds a write-off point; 30 is the final step of schedules A, B and C, so a scheduled price at or above it is the clearance price; a routine step below it never reopens a closed lot; a whole number from 1 to 100

model_id.note: GEMINI_MODEL overrides this deployment default; no model ID is hardcoded in agent code

location.note: VERTEX_LOCATION overrides this deployment default; global requires explicit configuration, never automatic 429 failover

seconds.source: 09-23 user decision, 2026-10-18 about 14:15 Bangkok, after observed paid checks: raise 25 to 40 seconds; fixed producer envelope includes retries and tools

max_tool_calls.source: 09-CONTEXT D-22: changing this limit requires the user's measured decision

max_llm_calls.source: 09-06; 09-RESEARCH Pattern 3: eight tools plus two model calls; explicit RunConfig resists ADK_MAX_LLM_CALLS

max_output_tokens.source: 09-23 observed user-run paid checks at b224c7f, 2026-10-18: accepted Ask output 1,372 plus thinking 1,754 = 3,126 tokens
max_output_tokens.note: Conservative per-response bound from the entire accepted request generation: twice 3,126, rounded up to the next power of two = 8,192; below documented model output ceiling 65,536. Small-sample safety margin, rerun pending.

max_request_tokens.source: 09-23 observed user-run paid checks at b224c7f, 2026-10-18: brief with 5 tools used 16,959 total tokens; the 6-tool question timed out before its second turn, so its full use is unobserved
max_request_tokens.note: supervisor margin: about 4x the observed maximum, so an 8-tool question is not cut by the token bound before the 40 s deadline; well inside the model context window

conditions.source: 06.1-UI-SPEC open questions 2 and 5 (recommended defaults, pending the user)
conditions.note: the condition a dispatch or receipt records (06.1 D-48)

resolutions.source: 06.1-UI-SPEC open questions 2 and 5 (recommended defaults, pending the user)
resolutions.note: how a receipt discrepancy is reconciled (06.1 D-65)
